notes:
POC focus: autoscaling and capacity management (scale-up/scale-down policies, warm pools, queueing behavior).
- Business context: Argent Helix runs fraud-detection + personalized offers in low-latency flow. Cannot tolerate long tail latency spikes during spikes (credit decisions).
- Targets: 500 QPS sustained for short chat/rerank flows; burst to 2k QPS for short windows. Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for 1-2k token requests (most traffic is 128-512 tokens).
- Throughput guarantees desired: committed baseline capacity to cover 500 QPS with headroom; ability to autoscale to 2x baseline within 30s; scale-down to baseline within 10m after idle.
- Warm pool ask: maintain 2-4 warm nodes (GPU instances) to reduce cold-start KV cache warmup; discuss warm-pool vs. per-request cache pre-loading. Team is worried about KV cache miss penalties on first request.
- Queueing/priority: want multi-tier queueing: high-priority (fraud checks) vs best-effort (analytics). Need request prioritization and preemption rules. Prefer server-side queue time < 50ms for high-priority.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask ~8x H100-equivalent GPUs (estimate) for baseline; prefer list of validated configurations and cost delta for z0/z1 zones. Procurement wants clear commitments and credit schedule.
- SLA negotiation items: 99.95% uptime for dedicated clusters, latency SLOs tied to credits, remedies for missed p95 SLOs; need agreement on measurement windows and synthetic probe locations.
- POC plan: 72h soak on dedicated pool (redwood-managed), synthetic + production shadow traffic (1% sampling), scale scenario scripts (gradual ramp, bursty spikes, recovery). Deliverables: throughput/latency heatmaps, cache warm-up curves, autoscale event logs, cost delta report.
- Security: must pass KMS integration test; audit log retention 2y; SSO via SAML (Okta). Data residency: US-only.
- Quotes from calls: "We can accept momentary queueing for batch jobs but fraud checks are non-negotiable". "Warm pool cost needs to be justified vs cold-start impact".
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (Sana Roy) - wants hard latency SLOs; Head of Infra (Liam Park) - focused on autoscale behavior and GPU ops; Procurement (Rita Gomez) - timeline end of Q4 for commit.
additional_notes_summary: Key eval axis: autoscaling responsiveness, warm-pool tradeoffs, predictable unit economics under reserved commitments. POC window agreed pending SLA draft.
